images.title: A quadrilateral as two triangles
images.purpose: Shows a diagonal splitting a quadrilateral into two triangles whose areas add.
images.composition: One quadrilateral, large and centred, with a horizontal diagonal.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. Quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal BD horizontal, 10 units long, B on the left and D on the right. Corner A is 4 units above BD, above the point 3.5 units from B; corner C is 3 units below BD, below the point 6 units from B. Triangle ABD (above) filled teal (#0072B2); triangle BCD (below) filled amber (#E69F00). Diagonal BD drawn thick dark. Two grey (#6B7280) dashed heights: from A straight down to BD and from C straight up to BD, each with a right angle mark. Labels: B, D at the ends; 10 cm along BD; 4 cm beside the upper height; 3 cm beside the lower height; 20 cm² inside the teal triangle; 15 cm² inside the amber triangle; Total 35 cm² below the figure. Check: 1/2 × 10 × 4 = 20, 1/2 × 10 × 3 = 15, 20 + 15 = 35.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: One diagonal turns a quadrilateral into two triangles; add their areas.
images.description: Shows a diagonal splitting a quadrilateral into two triangles whose areas add.
images.context: Matches the worked example: BD = 10 cm, heights 4 cm and 3 cm, area 35 cm².
images.teaching_notes: Both triangles share BD as base, so only the two heights are new.

image_decisions.why: The split into two triangles is the whole method, best seen as one coloured diagram.
